claims.why_not_priced: The evidence that this is unobserved is in the capture itself: 45 items, three stored bodies, and not one message, filing or news item between 2026-07-24 and the print - a five-week blackout in a name that moves a median 12% on prints. The decline that happened in that window therefore carries no information; the corpus's own commentary attributes it to short pressure and an absent market maker rather than to any datapoint. Meanwhile the thing that would matter - whether the back-to-school quarter turned profitable as the June commentary expected - is exactly what the print resolves, and no sell-side note, consensus figure or preview exists anywhere in the capture to set a bar against. The band is wide and crosses well into negative territory because this is a sub-$4 teen retailer with a -20.00% reaction in its record and because a no-debt balance sheet does not stop a comp miss.
claims.independence: From a different part of the corpus: filings.json independently shows the last company disclosure was an 8-K accepted 2026-06-11T23:23:03Z (accession 0001628280-26-042616, items 1.01 and 9.01, a material agreement) and nothing since, which corroborates that the run-in contains no company news rather than news I failed to find. A separate, weaker pointer in the same direction: recurring buyout speculation in the corpus on 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-24, unsupported by any filing.
